item.description:
Video effects, a new Program page, playbacks, and plot reading that checks itself

  • Video effects: video, picture, text and camera cues have an Effects tab: brightness, contrast, saturation (to black and white), hue, sepia, blur, vignette and a colour key for a green or blue screen, with ready-made looks. A fade cue's Effects toggle fades them (drift into black and white, blur out of focus), and fades a sound's built-in effects too (a reverb tail growing, a filter sweeping). The cue's own effects come back at its next GO.
  • Lighting, Program page: the keys are a full-height column on the right, the encoders run along the bottom, and the middle is four pools you choose from each pane's title tile (and how each looks: big or small tiles, a list, effects by type). Hide Keys (Tools menu, ⌃⌘K, the KEYS switch, or a MIDI pad) gives their space to more pools.
  • Playbacks view: ten faders to a page with GO, FLASH and REL, each holding a cue stack; every fader and button can be mapped to a MIDI controller and follows the page. TAP sets a tempo that effects can follow.
  • Effects: new Beam sweep (zoom, iris…) and Colour wave effects, a Fan knob that grows an effect along the lights, and Tempo to follow the tapped beat.
  • Light cues: right-click a cue in the cue sheet → Preview shows it on the plan and visualiser without touching the stage; Edit in Blind opens it in blind and Update goes into that cue.
  • Fixtures: Add Fixtures → New Type… makes a fixture type from its manual (starting from the one selected), saved on this Mac and exportable as GDTF; Request… asks for one or opens GDTF Share.
  • Import Rig: plots are now read from their own drawing lines, so each light is put on the pipe that actually runs through it (lights rated sure were right 9 times in 10 on nine venues' plots, up from 3 in 4). With the venue's paperwork, every light is checked against the plot: a strip says how many agree, disagree or are only on one side, and Review shows the differences side by side to choose from.
  • Exported plots now say Key to Fixtures.

A test show to try all of this (sound, video for a three-projector venue, and a lighting rig) comes as a separate folder.

Import a venue's rig: lights from the paperwork, positions from the plot

  • Patch → Import Rig…: choose the venue's channel hookup or instrument schedule (the PDF from Lightwright), a CSV or an exchange file, then Place Them from the Plot… and choose their plot PDF. Every light comes from the paperwork, exactly; each position it names ("#1 ELEC", "LX1", "DSR"…) is placed where the plot draws it, each bar as long as its pipe.
  • Starting from a plot instead: Add the Venue's Paperwork….
  • The positions list marks what to check: a question mark for a similar name or a boom (plots write a boom's name beside it), a dash for a position the plot doesn't show (left in a row to place by hand).
  • The plot is kept with the show and drawn under the stage plan, lined up, so you can see each position sits on its pipe. Plot beside the zoom buttons shows or hides it.

MIDI and key mapping, plug-ins, touch screens, rig import

  • MIDI and key mapping, the way Ableton Live does it: ⇧⌘M (or MIDI in the lighting window) tints every control you can map; click one, then move a knob, hit a pad or press a key (⇧⌘K for the Mac's keys). Faders take a range and pick up where they are; endless encoders work too. Setup → MIDI & Key Mappings… lists them; they're saved with the show.
  • Plug-ins: effects registered as music effects now show in Add Effect, and a new Plug-ins… button opens a searchable list of every Audio Unit effect on the Mac. If yours don't appear, it says why (Triskele reads Audio Units, not VST or AAX, and Logic's own effects aren't Audio Units), and the show log records what it found: please send that line if something's missing.
  • Touch screens: a TOUCH switch at the top of the lighting window (lit when on); more touch monitors are recognised by themselves; touch keys are bigger (about 50–60 pt).
  • Import Rig: lighting paperwork with two positions on one page (a "3rd Electric" heading under "2nd Strip") reads correctly. A plot PDF's lights can't be read reliably from the drawing, so for exact lights import the venue's channel hookup or instrument schedule (PDF), an MVR or a CSV. Try Reading the Drawing is there to experiment with: check every light it reads.
